rows.plainEnglishResponsibility: Approves presidential picks and helps make federal law.
rows.currentExample: The Senate confirmed Brooke Rollins as Agriculture Secretary, 72-28 (Feb. 13, 2025).

rows.plainEnglishResponsibility: Starts money bills and passes federal law.
rows.easyMetric: Bills passed / money bills started / hearings

rows.plainEnglishResponsibility: Runs the executive branch and can act fast with executive orders.
rows.currentExample: Trump signed an order creating the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud (Mar. 16, 2026).

rows.plainEnglishResponsibility: Runs state government and sets the state budget agenda.
rows.currentExample: Newsom proposed a $348.9B California budget for FY 2026-27 (Jan. 9, 2026).

rows.plainEnglishResponsibility: Writes and votes on state laws for one local district.
rows.easyMetric: Bills filed / committee seats / floor votes
rows.currentExample: Texas Rep. Brian Harrison had 75 bills listed in the 89th Legislature report (Mar. 18, 2026).

rows.plainEnglishResponsibility: Acts as the state's top lawyer and law enforcer.
rows.currentExample: New York AG Letitia James sued the Trump administration over tariffs (Mar. 5, 2026).

rows.plainEnglishResponsibility: Runs city departments and steers the city budget.
rows.currentExample: Mayor Mamdani released NYC's $127B FY 2027 preliminary budget (Feb. 17, 2026).
